entries.title: Psalms 69:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Waters - Tribulations.

entries.title: Psalms 69:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I restored - For peace sake.

entries.title: Psalms 69:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My sins - But O Lord, although I have been innocent to mine enemies, I am guilty of many sins and follies against thee.

entries.title: Psalms 69:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For my sake - Because of my sad disappointments. For if they see me forsaken, they will be discouraged by this example.

entries.title: Psalms 69:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For thy sake - For my obedience to thy commands, and zeal for thy glory.

entries.title: Psalms 69:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Zeal - That fervent love which I have for thy house and service, and glory, and people. Eaten - Exhausted my spirits. Upon me - I have been as deeply affected with thy reproaches, as with mine own. This tho' truly belonging to David, yet was also directed by the spirit of God in him, to represent the disposition and condition of Christ, in whom it was more fully accomplished, to whom therefore it is applied in the New Testament, the first part of it, John 2:17 , and the latter, Rom 15:3 .

entries.title: Psalms 69:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wept - For their impiety. Reproach - They derided me for it.

entries.title: Psalms 69:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Proverb - A proverb of reproach.

entries.title: Psalms 69:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: That sit - Vain and idle persons, that spend their time in the gates and markets.

entries.title: Psalms 69:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In the truth - Or, According to thy saving truth, or faithfulness; grant me that salvation, which thou hast graciously promised.

entries.title: Psalms 69:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Gall - Instead of giving me that comfort which my condition required, they added to my afflictions. Vinegar - These things were metaphorically fulfilled in David, but properly in Christ, the description of whose sufferings was principally intended here by the Holy Ghost.

entries.title: Psalms 69:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Their table - And this punishment in their table, exactly answers their sin, in giving Christ gall for his meat, ver. 21 . A snare - Their table or meat, which is set before them, shall become a snare: the occasion of their destruction.

entries.title: Psalms 69:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Eyes - Not the eyes of their bodies, but of their minds: as they that shut their eyes and will not see, so they shall be judicially blinded. To shake - To take away their strength.

entries.title: Psalms 69:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For - Which is an act of barbarous cruelty. Talk - Reproaching them, and triumphing in their calamities.

entries.title: Psalms 69:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wilt add - Give them up to their own lusts. Not let them - Partake of thy righteousness, or of thy mercy and goodness.

entries.title: Psalms 69:28
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Living - Of eternal life.

entries.title: Psalms 69:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: On high - Out of the reach of mine enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 69:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: This - This hearty sacrifice of praise, is more grateful to God, than the most glorious legal sacrifices. Hath horns - That is both tender and mature, as it is when the horns bud forth, and the hoofs grow hard.

entries.title: Psalms 69:32
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The humble - Those pious persons who are grieved for their calamities, will heartily rejoice in my deliverance. Live - Or, be revived, which were dejected, and in a manner dead with sorrow.

entries.title: Psalms 69:33
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Prisoners - Those who are in prison or affliction for his sake.

entries.title: Psalms 69:35
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sion - His church and people. They - His servants, as is explained in the following verse. There - In the literal Canaan for a long time, in the heavenly Canaan for ever.
